note: Answer key: expected Claims Analyst output for the KR adaptation of the UK report (synthetic). Truth values are filled by tools/claims.py.

claims.excerpt: from the perspective of the NHS and Personal Social Services
claims.rationale: Perspective becomes the local healthcare-system perspective (KR-S04).

claims.excerpt: Drug A is cost-effective
claims.rationale: Truth re-evaluated against the local reference value; the NICE range wording does not apply.

claims.excerpt: Drug A is not cost-effective
claims.rationale: The local setting has a single reference value, not a range (D09); a lower-bound statement has no meaning there.

claims.excerpt: the ICER was most sensitive to
claims.rationale: The global scenario set holds UK-specific values (e.g. the NICE non-reference discount rate); a local scenario set must be specified before rankings are regenerated.

claims.excerpt: is assumed to be the established standard of care in the NHS
claims.rationale: Whether the comparator is the local standard of care is a clinical question for local experts; it determines whether the comparison is relevant at all.

claims.excerpt: The analysis follows the NICE reference case
claims.rationale: Replace with the local guideline and perspective (KR-S04).

claims.excerpt: A confidential patient access scheme (PAS) discount is applied
claims.rationale: Local list prices are used and no risk-sharing agreement applies (KR-C15).

claims.excerpt: following the NICE Decision Support Unit guidance on survival analysis
claims.rationale: Keep as a methods citation, not as an agency requirement; cite the local guideline's survival-analysis expectations alongside it.

claims.excerpt: The fitted PFS and OS curves did not cross in either arm
claims.rationale: Efficacy is retained, so the check is expected to hold; the renderer re-checks it locally.

claims.excerpt: The cost of Drug B was taken from the electronic market information tool
claims.rationale: Cost sources become the local sources recorded in the input workbook (Source column).

claims.excerpt: All costs are in GBP
claims.rationale: Currency and price year come from the local inputs (KR-S02, KR-S03).

claims.excerpt: valued using the UK time trade-off value set
claims.rationale: Local state utilities use the Korean value set (KR-U01, KR-U02); the retained UK AE disutility and population norms must be tagged as retained (GAP-002, GAP-003).

claims.excerpt: PSA results are not included in this version
claims.rationale: Scope unchanged in the adaptation.

claims.excerpt: may differ slightly from values recalculated
claims.rationale: The renderer re-runs the rounding-interval check on the local tables and keeps the note only if required.

claims.excerpt: The largest single contributor to incremental costs was
claims.rationale: Rebuilt from the local cost breakdown.

claims.excerpt: partially offset its higher costs in other categories
claims.rationale: Rebuilt from the signs of the local incremental costs.

claims.excerpt: had the largest effect on the ICER
claims.rationale: Depends on a local scenario set (see C03).

claims.excerpt: remained below it in all other scenarios
claims.rationale: Depends on a local scenario set and the local reference value.

claims.excerpt: its effect on the ICER was negligible
claims.rationale: Under a Korean life table the cap may bind differently; the no-cap scenario must be run on the adapted model (switch via registry) before the wording is chosen.

claims.excerpt: Modelled medians were within the confidence intervals
claims.rationale: Refers to trial Kaplan-Meier confidence intervals that are not in the model; the efficacy is retained, so the statement can stay only if a person confirms the source.

claims.excerpt: should be reflected in the commissioning arrangements
claims.rationale: Commissioning is an NHS concept; the local equivalent is the reimbursement criteria (KR-C05).

claims.excerpt: Drug A can therefore be considered a cost-effective option
claims.rationale: Truth re-evaluated against the local reference value; the conclusion must not cite the NICE range or NHS resources.
